subject: Continuity planning: post-call summary & next actions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lind <ops@kestrelfinancial.com>; Kestrel Platform Team <platform@kestrelfinancial.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-14T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Continuity planning: post-call summary & next actions

Hi Sara / Kestrel team,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — appreciate the candid discussion. Below is a concise recap from our side to make sure we captured your priorities and to lay out suggested next steps. Please flag any corrections.

Recap — pain points and constraints
- Recent multi-region outage impacted customer-facing chat features for ~22 minutes (mid-March); unclear rollback & fallback behaviors executed by the platform.
- Need predictable degraded UX (short responses or cached answers) rather than full failure when model capacity spikes.
- Strict RTO expectation for the payments flow: you said ~5 minutes maximum impact for core flows.
- Strong requirement for separation of PII and auditability for requests routed to external models.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Primary model endpoints self-hosted on GCP (us-central1 + us-west1).
- In-house router with basic health checks; no automatic model-variant fallback.
- SLOs: internal target is 99.8% availability for critical endpoints; customer-facing acceptance TBD.

Success criteria (what Kestrel cares about)
- Visible fallbacks that preserve correctness for payment-related prompts.
- Audit log + token retention policy that meets compliance.
- Pilot demonstrating 50% reduction in customer-visible errors under load spikes.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) Kestrel: share two incident write-ups (we discussed one from March + one from Jan). Please attach by EOD Tue 4/15.
2) Redwood: deliver a short "continuity options" doc (3–4 pages) mapping fallbacks -> UX impact -> cost trade-offs by Fri 4/16. (Rishi owning technical options).
3) Quick pilot: 2-week pilot plan for a single payment flow in us-west1 with model-variant fallback and prefix caching. Proposed kickoff: week of 4/25.
4) Security/compliance: exchange SOC2 excerpts and data handling matrix. We attached a product sheet and our security matrix to start the thread.

Attachments: <Attachment: redwood_product_sheet.pdf>, <Attachment: security_matrix.xlsx>

If that lines up, I’ll schedule the pilot kickoff and loop in our infra team for an architecture review.

Thanks —
Ben

Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-14T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Continuity planning: post-call summary & next actions

Ben — thanks for the recap and the clear next steps. Confirming a few details and attaching the incident write-up from March (see attachment).

Quick clarifications / additions:
- Incident history:
  * 2027-03-12 (22m): model router misrouted a high-volume scheduled job to production pool, exhausted KV cache and caused head-of-queue spikes; failover was manual.
  * 2027-01-09 (45m): upstream GCP networking flake in us-central1 cascaded because there was no region-fallback enabled for the payments route.
- Must-have for pilot: the payment flow must never return a non-actionable response (e.g., "service unavailable") for basket checks. Instead, a deterministic fallback (short, cached summary with human-review flag) is acceptable.
- Compliance: we can share a redacted SOC2 summary and our data retention policy.

Attachment: <Attachment: kestrel_incident_report_q1.pdf>

I’ll get the second incident report to you by tomorrow EOD. The timeline for the pilot week of 4/25 works for us — please send a proposed agenda for the kickoff call so our SRE and security reps can attend.

—Sara
Sara Lind | Head of Ops, Kestrel Financial
ops@kestrelfinancial.com | +1 (212) 555-4446

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lind <ops@kestrelfinancial.com>, Kestrel Platform Team <platform@kestrelfinancial.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T07:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Continuity planning: post-call summary & next actions

Thanks for the details, Sara — helpful. Following up with concrete technical options we can include in the continuity options doc: (high-level, will flesh in the PDF)

Option A — Regional model-fallback + graceful-text-truncation
- Keep primary model in us-central1; if health checks fail, route to smaller quantized variant in us-west1.
- UX: return shorter deterministic responses for sensitive payment checks; include a human-review flag.
- Pros: small latency increase when fallback used; deterministic behavior reduces randomness.

Option B — Prefix caching for payment intents + degraded-mode egress
- Cache validated payment intent responses for N minutes; on spike, serve cache + mark as cached.
- Pros: near-zero latency during spikes for common intents; preserves correctness for most flows.

Option C — Canary routing + token-based throttles
- Canary new model variants under low load; apply strict token quotas for background jobs to reduce risk of scheduled-jobs starving production.

SLO suggestions for pilot (proposal)
- Payment checks: 99.9% successful, where "successful" = returned actionable (non-failure) response within 700ms median; still allow degraded-mode under extreme load with notification.
- Observability: per-request tracing + token-level cost breakdown for pilot.

I attached a draft continuity options deck (continuity_options_v1.pdf) that maps UX trade-offs and estimated infra changes. If the team likes Option B + A as fallback strategy, we can scope the pilot runbook and required infra changes by Wed 4/20.

Attachment: <Attachment: continuity_options_v1.pdf>

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Sara Lind <ops@kestrelfinancial.com>

Date: 2027-04-15T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Continuity planning: post-call summary & next actions

Rishi / Ben — this is great, thanks. Option B (prefix caching) + Option A for region fallback sounds like the right balance for us.

Confirming next items from Kestrel:
- We will send the second incident write-up today.
- Our SRE and security leads can join the kickoff call on 4/26 (can do morning PT).
- We want the pilot acceptance criteria spelled out: exact latency windows and the list of intents considered "payment-critical."

Ben — please schedule the kickoff for 4/26 morning PT and share the pilot acceptance doc ahead of the call. Monica / Rishi — happy to coordinate a pre-kickoff architecture sync if useful.

—Sara
